page: Microsoft Azure DC48ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processors managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 48 virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled at two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 192.0 GB, delivering a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The processor configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, 32 MB of L3 cache, and instruction support for AVX-512 vector extensions including VNNI and BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI.

The instance includes 1933 GB of integrated local SSD storage alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. Hardware accelerators are not present, with zero dedicated GPUs assigned to the configuration. Network connectivity does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring auxiliary virtual networking provisioning for direct external routing.

Benchmark evaluations show strong CPU compute capabilities. In stress-ng testing, the server achieved a single-core score of 3023.97 and a multi-core score of 72107.5, placing both metrics within the top 25% tier. In-memory data throughput evaluated via Redis SET operations registered 60.32 million operations per second, ranking within the middle 50% percentile.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the provision of bundled 1.93 TB local solid-state storage reduces dependencies on external block devices for high-speed scratch space or temporary caches. The combination of balanced memory density, AVX-512 instruction support, and strong multi-core execution profile makes the DC48ads_v6 effective for containerized application microservices, database clusters, intermediate data transformations, and distributed compilation workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure DC48ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 48-vCPU AMD EPYC 9V74 processor across 24 physical cores with hyperthreading. It features 192.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 1933 GB of local SSD temporary storage with support for Premium Storage tiers. Compute benchmarks reflect strong results, with stress-ng single-core achieving 3023.97 and multi-core reaching 72107.5, both ranking in the top 25% of tested systems. Memory and transactional caching performance is solid, evidenced by Redis SET operations reaching 60.32 million operations per second. Lacking dedicated GPUs and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the instance is structured for dense general workloads. Its hardware profile and bundled high-capacity NVMe-grade local storage render it practical for relational databases, enterprise web applications, distributed build systems, and intermediate data processing pipelines.
